ruleset.name: nitpicker-spring
ruleset.description: Nitpicker Spring rules: one allowed way for dependency injection, proxies, web, JPA and Spring Data.

rule.name: SpringConstructorInjection
rule.message: Inject through the constructor into private final fields. Do not put @Autowired, @Inject, @Resource or @Value on fields or setters.

rule.message: Make this field of a bean final, static fields too. Beans are shared singletons, so keep per-call state in locals.

rule.name: SpringLiteConfiguration
rule.message: Write @Configuration(proxyBeanMethods = false) and take dependencies as @Bean method parameters instead of calling other @Bean methods.

rule.name: SpringNoComponentScan
rule.message: Put the @SpringBootApplication class in the top package and let it scan its own packages; do not add @ComponentScan or scanBasePackages.

rule.name: SpringTypedConfiguration
rule.message: Read configuration through a @ConfigurationProperties record and pass the values in through constructors or parameters, not @Value, System.getenv, System.getProperty or Environment.getProperty. JVM properties such as java.*, user.*, javax.*, jdk.* and http.* are fine.

rule.name: SpringProfileOnConfiguration
rule.message: Put @Profile only on a @Configuration class or a @Bean method, so profiles choose beans and never branch business code.

rule.name: SpringBeanCollectionState
rule.message: Fill a plain collection of a shared singleton bean only at startup (the constructor, @PostConstruct or afterPropertiesSet) and keep it as Map.copyOf or List.copyOf, or use a ConcurrentHashMap or a cache (@Cacheable). Changed after startup, request threads would write to it at once.

rule.name: SpringHttpClientPerCall
rule.message: Build the HTTP client once, from the injected RestClient.Builder or RestTemplateBuilder, and keep it in a final field or a @Bean. A client built in each call throws away its connection pool.

rule.message: Move startup work that calls a database or a remote service out of @PostConstruct into an ApplicationRunner or an @EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent). @PostConstruct runs before the context is ready: there is no transaction around this call, other beans may not be proxied yet, and a failure stops the application from starting.
